title: A Locker for the Group Chat
premise: Bram Amberdale, a scholarship student at Hollowmere Academy, is paired for a semester project with his nemesis, Sable Voss, whose family sits on the school board. Digging into the school's archives for their assignment, they uncover evidence that the board buried a scandal years ago — a student who vanished before her final audition, erased from every record. As Bram and Sable's uneasy alliance deepens into something like trust, they realize the board will silence anyone who gets close to the truth, and that Sable's own family helped bury it. At the final audition, Bram exposes the buried records publicly, forcing resignations and costing him his scholarship — but earning back the vanished student's name, and a future he chooses for himself.
about_author: Elodie Fairweather is a former boarding-school scholarship kid who writes about institutions, memory, and the students institutions forget. She lives near the coast, where she collects old yearbooks and refuses to throw any of them away.

chapters.title: Counting Days
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. He maps his survival strategy at Hollowmere: stay invisible, keep grades perfect, graduate. Establishes his scholarship precarity and quiet resentment of wealthy classmates. Emotional beat: weary resignation cracked by a flicker of ambition when he sees the spring audition poster.

chapters.title: Assigned
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The history teacher announces semester-long archival projects and pairs Bram with Sable Voss, his tormentor since freshman year. They argue in front of the class; the teacher refuses to budge. Beat: humiliation sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Alternating Bram/Sable. Their first research session in the basement archive is cold war — until Sable finds a box misfiled under a wrong year, containing an audition program missing one name. Beat: reluctant curiosity overriding hostility.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She recognizes the handwriting on the box as her late aunt's — a former Hollowmere star. She begins investigating alone at night, hiding it from Bram while pretending the project is dead. Beat: guilt and inherited shame.

chapters.title: Truce Terms
chapters.summary: Bram catches Sable sneaking out of the archive. Instead of reporting her, she offers a deal: find the truth together, split the credit. Beat: wary partnership sealed over bad vending-machine coffee.

chapters.title: Redacted
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. They request official records and receive pages so heavily redacted they're useless — signed off by Sable's uncle, a current board member. First hint someone is watching them. Beat: dread arriving quietly.

chapters.title: The Yearbook Gap
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Comparing yearbooks, they find a photo cropped mid-frame and a blank page where a senior tribute should be. A retired groundskeeper mentions 'the girl who fell.' Beat: grief for a stranger neither ever met.

chapters.title: Detention
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Both are given detention on fabricated vandalism charges — clearly retaliation. In detention they compare notes properly for the first time and map the board's families. Beat: solidarity forged under unfair punishment.

chapters.title: Sable's House
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Bram visits the Voss estate for a 'project session' and finds her aunt's locked music room, preserved like a shrine. Her grandmother catches them; her warning is ambiguous — protective or threatening. Beat: fear wearing a polite face.

chapters.title: What the Scholarship Buys
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The headmaster offers Bram a full-ride extension — if his project 'stays within approved materials.' He realizes he's being bought and doesn't tell Sable. Beat: temptation and self-disgust.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Hidden in the aunt's sheet music, a letter: the aunt discovered the board was falsifying admissions and safety reports; days later she was gone, ruled an accident. Beat: horror hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Split
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Sable discovers Bram accepted the meeting with the headmaster without telling her and accuses him of selling out. Their partnership shatters. Beat: betrayal — earned, mutual, painful.

chapters.title: Alone With It
chapters.summary: Alternating short sections. Bram, wracked, copies the letter and evidence to a hidden drive; Sable confronts her uncle, who admits nothing but looks afraid. Beat: two people deciding separately what they're willing to lose.

chapters.title: The Second Name
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Following the money trail, they learn the vanished girl wasn't the only one — three students across decades were scrubbed after complaining. Beat: scale of the corruption revealed; stakes become systemic.

chapters.title: Locked Doors
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Bram's dorm is searched; his drive goes missing. Someone leaks that Sable is 'unstable,' echoing what was said about her aunt. Beat: the machinery of erasure turning toward them.

chapters.title: The Groundskeeper's Testimony
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The retired groundskeeper, dying, gives a recorded account of the night the girl died — and who ordered the cleanup. Beat: solemn passing of the torch from one silenced witness to two new ones.

chapters.title: Reconciliation
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Bram confesses why he took the offer — terror of losing everything — and returns the copied evidence he'd secretly kept. They rebuild trust deliberately, naming rules. Beat: forgiveness as a choice, not a feeling.

chapters.title: Audition Week
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The board moves the audition up, hoping to run out the clock. Security follows them; Sable's family threatens to have her committed to 'rest.' Beat: pressure peaking, plan crystallizing.

chapters.title: The Final Audition
chapters.summary: Both POVs interwoven. Before a packed hall including donors and press, Bram performs — then stops mid-piece and reads the aunt's letter aloud as Sable broadcasts the unredacted records to every screen in the building. Beat: climax; courage as public, irreversible act.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Resignations cascade; police reopen the case. Sable's uncle implicates her grandmother, fracturing the family beyond repair. Beat: victory that costs more than expected.

chapters.title: The Price
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. His scholarship is revoked retroactively; the school offers hush money. He refuses, plans to transfer to a state school, and restores the erased students' names to a memorial plaque himself. Beat: grief and integrity entwined.

chapters.title: A Locker for the Group Chat
chapters.summary: Final chapter, both POVs converging. Graduation day: Bram walks not as a survivor of Hollowmere but as its conscience. Sable leaves too, carrying her aunt's sheet music. Last image: the group chat renamed, the locker opened, nothing hidden anymore. Beat: bittersweet freedom.
